title: Arnica bruise balm
subtitle: A yellow, calendula-and-arnica infused balm for bruises and bumps
excerpt: A firm beeswax balm made on an arnica and calendula infused oil. Traditionally applied to bruises, sprains, and sore muscles, not for broken skin. Gives about 100 g of balm in a small tin. Shelf life 12 months.
sourceNotes: Arnica montana in topical preparations: traditional use documented in Commission E monograph (1988) and EMA HMPC monograph (2014) for bruises, sprains, and minor muscle soreness. Not for broken or abraded skin. Calendula officinalis infused oil as the carrier: anti-inflammatory co-constituent and a traditional pairing with arnica in folk pharmacopoeias. Beeswax-to-oil ratio for a firm salve: 1 part beeswax to 4 parts infused oil by weight.

recipe.batchNotes: Scales directly. Doubling to a 200 ml tin works cleanly; adjust the beeswax proportionally for the same firmness.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The infused oil can be made weeks ahead and stored in a dark bottle. The finished balm is ready to use once set.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: 12 months in a cool, dark cupboard. Anhydrous balms are stable without a preservative. Discard if the balm smells rancid or the surface develops white spots.

glossaryTerms.definition: A preparation that contains no water phase. Anhydrous balms like this one are shelf-stable without a preservative because there is no moisture for micro-organisms to grow in.
A carrier oil in which dried plant material has been steeped, here, arnica flowers and calendula petals steeped in sunflower oil, to extract fat-soluble constituents.

content.text: Arnica bruise balm is a firm beeswax salve made on an oil infused with dried arnica flowers and calendula petals. It goes on sore, bruised, or aching skin, on the muscle or the body part, not on broken skin or open wounds. The balm has a slightly yellow tinge from the calendula. About 100 g of finished balm; ready to use once set; keeps 12 months.
Important
Do not apply arnica preparations to broken skin, open cuts, or wounds. Arnica is for external use on intact skin only. Discontinue use if any skin irritation, redness, or rash develops.
Ingredients

items.prepNote: dried Arnica montana flowers; for infusing into the carrier oil
dried calendula petals; infused alongside the arnica
carrier oil for infusing both herbs; yields ~80 g strained oil
yellow cosmetic-grade beeswax; sets the infused oil into a firm balm

content.text: Method
Make the infused oil (3-4 weeks ahead)
Pack the dried arnica flowers and calendula petals into a clean glass jar. Pour the sunflower oil over them until fully submerged, with about 1 cm of oil above the plant material.
Seal and leave in a warm, dark place for 3-4 weeks, shaking daily. Strain through a muslin cloth, pressing the plant material to extract all the oil. Measure out 80 g of the strained
infused oil
for the balm.
Make the balm
Combine 80 g of the infused oil and the beeswax in a heatproof bowl over a saucepan of simmering water (or in a double boiler). Heat gently until the beeswax is fully melted.
To test firmness, drip a few drops onto a cold saucer. If it sets too soft, add more beeswax a gram at a time and retest; too firm, add a teaspoon of oil and retest.
Pour into the tin. Leave undisturbed for 2 hours until fully set.
Patch test
Apply a small amount to the inside of the forearm and wait 24 hours before using on a larger area. Arnica and calendula can cause contact allergy in people sensitive to daisy-family plants.
Storage and shelf life
Keep the tin in a cool, dark cupboard. The
anhydrous
balm keeps 12 months. Discard if the balm develops a rancid smell or white spots on the surface.
